sections.heading: See every feed account (agents)
sections.text: GET /connections/inventory (read scope) lists every account SimpleFIN delivers, grouped by bank login, whether or not a ledger account takes it: the login's error, and per account the ledger account it feeds (or none), how many days old its bank balance is (stale past feed stale days), how many holdings and transactions the latest sync carried, and any account error. It answers "did my new account show up?" without admin rights. API tokens without admin scope never see SimpleFIN ids, and the masked account numbers banks put in names ((1234), 1234) are removed. Agents use the MCP tool feed status: one line per bank login plus only the accounts that need attention (not connected, stale Nd, an error code). An ignored account is not reported as not connected.

sections.heading: Sync schedule and the fetch budget
sections.text: The schedule is a runtime setting in Settings - Connections (not an environment variable): daily at a time you choose (06:30 by default), every 12h , every 6h , or hourly . The interval presets land a run just before the matching job. SimpleFIN Bridge allows 24 fetches per day ; the hourly preset sits exactly at that budget, and the per-connection guard fails soft beyond it. Each run starts at a random point in the 10 minutes after its slot, as SimpleFIN asks apps to spread their fetches. Agents should call trigger sync when the user wants fresh data, not on every question. The daily time is a clock time in the household time zone (PURSER TIMEZONE, Settings - General ), stored as the hour and minute of sync schedule in PUT /config, and the scheduler reads it in that zone. It stays at the same time on the clock when daylight saving starts or ends: 06:30 in New York is 06:30 in winter and in summer. On the night the clocks change, a time the clocks skip runs an hour later and a time in the repeated hour runs twice. Changing the household time zone keeps the clock time and moves the sync to the new zone. The interval presets run on fixed UTC times. Members (read + write) see each connection's summary, its banks and accounts, Sync now and, under Maintenance and schedule , Fetch older history and Re-fetch a date range . Bank balances, the comparison with Purser, Map and Ignore , adding a connection and the schedule are admin-only. The schedule, older history, re-fetching, the comparison basis and adding a connection all sit under Maintenance and schedule at the foot of the page. Every request asks for at most 45 days, the span SimpleFIN recommends: a first sync (88 days) takes two requests, and a long backfill, an outage repair or a refetch takes one request per 45 days. Each counts against the daily budget.

sections.heading: Pending transactions
sections.text: Banks report a charge as pending before it posts, and Purser imports it as a pending row. Every sync re-checks each open pending on a checking, savings, cash or credit card account against the bank, not only the last week's: the fetch reaches back to the oldest such pending (and a week before it), up to 44 days (one request within the Bridge's recommended 45 days). Pendings on brokerage, loan and property (asset) accounts never stretch the fetch: some investment feeds list every purchase as pending indefinitely, and those accounts are valued by holdings, valuations or the reported balance anyway. They are still settled whenever the fetch covers their dates. - When the bank posts it, the posted row replaces the pending, whether it arrives with a new description or date or with the very same ones. - When a pending disappears, Purser first looks for its posted row: same account, same amount, dated within 7 days either way. - A pending the bank dropped with no posted row is voided and emits a pending.vanished event. The whats new digest counts these and lists the ones above its materiality threshold. A dropped refund is worth chasing. A pending older than 44 days no longer widens the fetch and stays as it is unless a backfill or refetch covers its date. Void it yourself if your bank no longer shows it.

sections.heading: Re-described rows
sections.text: A fetch that reaches back past the last week also brings older posted rows the ledger already holds. Banks sometimes rewrite a posted row's description weeks later (a merchant name gains a suffix, say), and because the description is part of a row's identity, that copy would otherwise land as a second row. Purser skips it as re-described when the account already has a posted row from an earlier sync on the same date for the same amount, under a description the bank no longer lists. Sync and backfill results count these as skipped redescribed. A row that posted late with no such neighbour imports normally, and so does a row a disappearing pending may have posted as.

sections.heading: Backfill older history
sections.text: The first sync reaches 88 days back. To page older history, use Fetch older history under Maintenance and schedule in Settings - Connections (or POST /connections/{id}/backfill, write scope). Backfill walks backward in windows of at most 45 days (the Bridge's recommended span), archiving each verbatim, and latches complete after four consecutive empty windows (180 days with nothing). It never moves the forward sync anchor, shares the daily fetch budget (reserving two fetches for scheduled and manual syncs), and resumes from a saved cursor if interrupted. A result may carry a qif overlap warning when a backfilled range meets manually imported rows; identical rows still dedup by content hash. You can scope a backfill to specific accounts so onboarding one need not re-fetch the rest.

sections.heading: Scope an account with feed_start
sections.text: accounts.feed start is a per-account date: the importer skips feed rows dated strictly before it, across sync, backfill, and map re-import alike. Set it to partition an account's history cleanly — manual import owns everything before the boundary, the feed owns everything on or after it. It is import-time only: setting it never deletes rows already in the ledger, and skips are counted as skipped before feed start. Set it via PATCH /accounts/{id} (an explicit null clears it). The typical rollout is to set it at the manual/feed boundary when you first map the account.

sections.heading: Fix a sign-inverted feed with feed_invert
sections.text: Some institutions deliver an account's transaction stream with the signs flipped — deposits arriving as negative amounts (observed with Fidelity brokerage, HSA, and 401(k) accounts). The symptoms are an asset account whose balance trends negative and transfers that never pair (both legs carry the same sign). Set accounts.feed invert via PATCH /accounts/{id} (admin, like feed start) and the importer negates every feed amount for that account from then on. The inversion happens after content hashing, so a row's identity stays exactly what the bank sent: flipping the flag never re-imports history, and rows already in the ledger are never rewritten — repairing existing wrong-signed rows is a separate, deliberate admin operation.

sections.heading: Loan balances come from valuations
sections.text: A loan or mortgage feed often reports a balance but few or no transactions. Purser records each reported balance for a loan account as a row in that account's valuations series, and every balance surface — the accounts list, the account page headline, GET /accounts/{id}/balance, and the agent tools — reports the latest valuation as the account's balance (balance method: "valuation", with balance as of naming the valuation date). When the feed does deliver transactions they stay visible in the register as ordinary postings history, and the postings sum rides along as postings balance. An account with no valuation yet falls back to the postings sum. Net worth uses the same rule, so the account page and net worth always agree. An account mapped as property is a ledger instead: when its reported balance differs from its balance on the sync's day, Purser posts a value change for the difference (see Track a house or other asset).

sections.heading: Brokerage balances add holdings to cash
sections.text: A brokerage feed reports cash transactions and a holdings snapshot side by side. Purser stores each as what it is — cash movements become ordinary postings, holdings become rows in holdings snapshots — and every balance surface reports the two added together : the postings sum plus the market value of the latest holdings snapshot at or before the date you asked about (balance method: "postings+holdings", with balance as of naming the snapshot date). The cash-only figure rides along as postings balance. The difference from a loan is that a valuation replaces the postings sum while a market value adds to it — a brokerage account's cash is real money the feed already told you about, so dropping it would understate the account. An account with no snapshot yet reports the postings sum alone, and a closed account keeps its postings answer so a stale snapshot cannot resurrect it. Net worth uses the same rule, so the account page and net worth agree here too. See Balances for all three methods and the two bases they are applied to.

sections.heading: When the feed sends no holdings
sections.text: Some brokerage feeds deliver the account's cash but no holdings at all. Switch such an account's holdings source to manual (admin, PATCH /accounts/{id} with {"holdings source": "manual"}) and record its positions by hand: the feed keeps importing the cash, stops recording holdings for that account (holdings skipped manual in the sync result), and the positions you record are priced daily and added to the balance the same way. See Track holdings by hand.

sections.heading: Watch accounts converge
sections.text: Settings - Connections shows an admin, per account, the bank's balance and its date and a Compared with Purser column (matches, or how far off), from GET /connections/{id}/discovered, recomputed live from the latest archived payload. How balances are compared , under Maintenance and schedule , lists both balances and the drift side by side. It is the convergence meter while you onboard or backfill — expect drift to shrink toward zero as history fills in. After every successful sync, Purser also runs a balance-drift check that emits a balance.drift event when a mapped cash or card account's reported balance disagrees with the ledger. It is a warning only : it never fails a sync, never adjusts the ledger, and never writes financial rows. See Events and webhooks for the event, and whats new for the agent-facing digest. When the drift is real and you have the statement balance, reconcile the account. Banks differ on whether the balance they report counts pending charges, so the drift is measured on the basis each account's bank uses, reported as drift basis and shown next to the drift: posted only when the bank leaves pendings out, pending inclusive otherwise. Purser learns the basis per account from its recent syncs (the one whose drift held steady wins), so a standing gap at a bank that leaves pendings out stays one number while charges come and go instead of moving with every pending. The same basis rides on the balance.drift event (mode) and on each whats new drift line (basis). An account's first syncs have nothing to learn from yet, so the smaller of the two drifts decides until its history tells them apart. The ledger balance column always includes pendings. A brokerage account's feed balance is usually its total value, so brokerage accounts are left out of the check. The exception is a cash sweep whose positions you track by hand: an admin can say its feed balance is its cash (PATCH /accounts/{id} with {"feed balance is cash": true}, or Feed balance is cash on the account page), and the account is then checked like a checking account. See Track holdings by hand.

sections.heading: Pin an account's drift basis
sections.text: When an account's history is short or misleading, pin its basis by hand: the Basis select under Maintenance and schedule - How balances are compared offers Auto (showing the basis Purser learned) and the two pins. Over the API, an admin sends PATCH /accounts/{id} with {"drift basis override": "posted only"} or "pending inclusive"; null clears the pin and absent leaves it alone. Only checking, savings, cash and credit-card accounts take a pin (the drift check runs on nothing else), and the change is audited. A pinned basis wins over the learned one everywhere it is reported: GET /connections/{id}/discovered sets drift basis pinned (and still shows the learned pick as drift basis learned), the balance.drift event carries basis pinned: true, and the whats new drift line carries pinned: true. The pin only chooses which drift is reported: an account whose bank balance matches either basis is still in sync. Purser keeps learning underneath the pin, so clearing it brings back exactly the basis its history picks. Because setting or clearing a pin changes the reported drift, it can open one new balance.drift episode. The authoritative spec is DESIGN.md sections 7.1 (connect, backfill, feed start) and 7.3 (balance-drift check).

pages.title: Suggestions inbox
pages.description: Decide what Purser thinks you should do — detected recurring bills and transfers, agent-proposed schedules, transfer-link rules your confirms propose, bill matches the matcher proposes, bank rows that look like one transfer — from the Dashboard cards or the MCP tools.

sections.text: A suggestion is something Purser thinks you should decide: a recurring payee it found in your history, a schedule an agent proposed, a payment for a card you just added, a rule to link a transfer you keep confirming by hand, a bank row the matcher thinks paid one of your expected bills, or two bank rows that look like one transfer between your accounts. It carries a typed draft of what it would create, the evidence behind it, a confidence where Purser scored one, and it remembers what you decided. The Dashboard cards and the MCP tools are two renderings of the same rows. Every suggestion has a kind, and the kind decides what its draft is: Kind Draft Accepting it creates --- --- --- schedule a schedule (name, account, rrule, amount, ...) an active schedule, materialized immediately transfer link a transfer link rule for one account pair, scoped to a payee the rule as a draft , which links nothing until you activate it match an expected row and the bank row the matcher proposed for it, with both amounts and the variance the confirmed match : the bill is paid by that row transfer pair two bank rows of exactly opposite amounts on two of your accounts, close in date, that nothing links on its own the transfer : one transaction in place of the two rows

sections.heading: Where suggestions come from
sections.text: - Detection. The nightly detector (07:05 UTC), POST /schedules/detect or MCP detect schedules scans your history per account and counterparty — payees for ordinary bills, the other account for transfers — for recurring cadences (weekly to yearly, including semi-monthly paydays). Each pattern becomes one suggestion — never a schedule — with a confidence that reflects how much evidence there is, how regular the gaps are and how steady the amount is. Running detection again refreshes the open row (its seen count climbs) instead of creating a duplicate. - Agents. A create schedule call with propose=true lands here with the draft the agent asked for, source = agent. It has no confidence, because nothing scored it, so it lists after the scored suggestions. The agent can attach a note of up to 200 characters, such as the statement line it read, and the card shows it. If the account already has a schedule for that payee or counterparty (active, paused or ended), the proposal is refused with a 422 that names the schedule, so the inbox never holds a duplicate of it. - A new liability account (card, loan) triggers a scan for payments to it — merged transfers to the account and one-sided outflows whose payee names it — and lands them as source = account added. - A manual transfer confirm. When you merge two bank rows with confirm transfer (MCP) or POST /matching/confirm-transfer, Purser proposes a transfer link rule for that account pair, scoped to the payee on the rows, as source = confirm. Confirming another pair of the same accounts and payee refreshes the same suggestion — its evidence is the pairs you confirmed — instead of adding one. A split loan payment proposes nothing, and neither does a pair whose rows carry no payee. See Manage transfers. - The matcher. When the nightly matching pass (or POST /matching/run) scores a bank row in the middle tier for an expected bill — close, but not sure enough to match on its own — it proposes the match and the proposal appears here as a match card (source = detected, the match score as its confidence). The card only mirrors the proposal: confirming or rejecting it in an account register, or marking the bill paid with that row, decides the card too, and when the proposal goes away on its own — the bank drops the pending row, the row merges into a transfer, a better row settles the bill — the card is withdrawn . A bank row matched to an expected transfer waits a few days for its other leg before it gets a card, because the transfer usually settles it by itself. See How matching works. - Transfer candidates. After each import and the nightly matching job, two bank rows that leave one account and arrive in another with exactly the same amount, at most 3 days apart, but carry no keyword, rule or schedule that links them, become a transfer pair card (source = detected, no confidence: amount and date are all there is to go on). Only pairs whose two sides have both posted, the newer in the last 60 days, get a card, so importing years of history does not flood the inbox; older pairs stay flagged in the account register, and a pair with a side still pending waits until both post. Linking the pair with the register's Link ⇄ (or confirm transfer) accepts its card, and its ✗ rejects it; when the pair stops being a candidate any other way — a rule or keyword links it, an [account] edit or the categorize pass pairs a row elsewhere, a side is voided or matched to a bill — the card is withdrawn (a conversion's withdrawal is audited with the reason transfer.convert). When the categorize pass corrects one of the rows (a posted row gets a reversal and a replacement), the card stays the same card, snooze included, and names the replacement. See Manage transfers.

sections.heading: Reviewing Needs attention
sections.text: The Dashboard lists Expected payments not seen before suggestions. Each expectation shows its account, amount, age and available estimate or paused schedule labels. A past expected date is a prompt to check the bank statement; it does not prove a missed payment. A paused schedule can retain an explicitly confirmed or pinned occurrence; inspect it before deciding what to do. Suggestions are collapsed into Payment matches , Possible transfers , Recurring schedules and Transfer rules . Filter by account (either side of a transfer), choose oldest first or strongest pattern first, then expand a group. Pages contain ten suggestions. Pattern strength is a heuristic evidence score, not a probability; "checked" counts detector runs, not transactions. Evidence dates link to the underlying records. The action names state what they do: Confirm payment match , Link as transfer , Create schedule , or Create draft rule . Inspect the records before confirming. A schedule editor offers monthly, weekly, two-week and four-week choices and preserves custom recurrence rules. A created schedule can be edited or paused in Scheduled transactions; matches and transfers can be undone in the register. A transfer rule still requires its separate activation preview. Transaction review shows per-account links for posted and pending rows. In a register, select posted transactions and choose Review selected to preview their dates, payees, amounts and categories before confirming the review marks. Pending rows and other pages are excluded. Global counts count a transfer once; account counts include both sides. Agent proposals are shown separately. The REST summary is GET /transactions/review-summary (read scope). A failed check shows an incomplete-results message and Retry. All clear appears only after every attention check succeeds and every group is empty.

sections.heading: Detection safeguards
sections.text: Four-week patterns use a weekly recurrence with interval four when repeated 28-day gaps and calendar drift support it. Calendar-month patterns retain monthly recurrence. Opposite-sign entries are not combined into one recurring cash flow. When a previously stable series has a changed latest amount, the proposal shows that latest amount and asks you to verify the possible price change; it may instead be a one-time adjustment. Detector-owned schedule cards are hidden when their evidence has lapsed. A completed detection scan withdraws patterns no longer supported by current history, with an audit entry. If the pattern returns, the same withdrawn card can reopen; accepted and rejected decisions remain durable. Agent-authored proposals are not expired by this detector. Stale automatic proposals must be refreshed before acceptance. Match cards and their counts require a live proposal and live transaction rows, and show variance from current signed amounts. Positive rows explicitly described as refunds, cash-back/reward credits, dividends or earned-interest credits are excluded from amount-and-date-only transfer candidates. You can still explicitly link a mislabeled bank row. Loan and investment recurrence proposals require particular care: inspect both accounts and the evidence to distinguish a cash movement from an internal allocation. These safeguards use transaction evidence, not merchant-specific or household-specific exceptions.

sections.heading: Deciding
sections.text: POST /suggestions/{id}/decide or MCP decide suggestion, write scope: Decision Effect --- --- accept Applies the draft exactly as shown. A schedule becomes an active schedule, materialized immediately; a transfer link becomes a draft rule (below); a match confirms the match, which also marks the bank row reviewed; a transfer pair links the two rows as one transfer, exactly as confirming them in the register does — the response's transfer names the merged row and, when the confirm proposed one, the transfer link suggestion for that pair and payee. edit then accept Same, after merging your edits. A schedule takes any draft field — name, rrule, dtstart, amount, amount type, estimate basis, payee, category, counterparty account, autopost policy. A transfer link takes only what narrows or widens it — amount exact (a decimal string), window days (0 to 14) and effective from — because its account pair and payee are what it proposes. A match has nothing to edit: to pay the bill with a different row, mark it paid with that row (POST /matching/match, MCP match). A transfer pair has nothing to edit either: to link other rows, confirm them (POST /matching/confirm-transfer, MCP confirm transfer). The edits are validated by the same schema before anything is created. reject Durable. reject scope = counterparty means "never suggest this payee or counterparty on this account again" — for a transfer link, never again for this account pair, whatever the payee; exact (default) rejects just this pattern, or this pair and payee. A match is rejected exactly: the matcher never proposes that bank row for that bill again, nor the posted row that replaces it when it was pending. A transfer pair is rejected exactly too: "not a transfer" — nothing links those two rows automatically again, not even a rule you activate later. snooze Hides it until snooze until (default 30 days). Nothing auto-accepts on expiry — it simply returns to the inbox. A snoozed match stays proposed: its bank row is still held, and the forecast still counts the bill as paid pending your confirmation. Deciding a match card whose proposal is already gone answers 422 and withdraws the card, and so does deciding a transfer pair whose rows no longer pair (one was linked elsewhere, voided or matched to a bill).

sections.heading: Accepting a transfer link
sections.text: A transfer-link suggestion never links anything by itself, and accepting it does not either. Accepting creates the rule as a draft and returns projected links: how many of your past pairs the rule would link if you activated it now. Activation is the rule's own confirm step — the Dashboard card asks it right after you accept, the Rules page offers it for every draft, and over REST it is POST /rules/{rule id}/state with {"state": "active", "confirm links": N}. An agent can accept with decide suggestion, but there is no MCP tool to activate the rule: the count confirm happens on the Dashboard card, the Rules page or over REST. See Activating a pair rule for why the count is asked for. On the Dashboard each open suggestion is a card: the headline, its source and confidence, an evidence summary that expands into the occurrences (or, for a transfer link, the pairs you confirmed), and the four decisions (rejecting asks whether to reject just this one or never suggest the pair again). GET /suggestions lists the open inbox by confidence, a page at a time (limit, at most 25, and offset for the next page) — ?kind=schedule, ?kind=transfer link, ?kind=match or ?kind=transfer pair narrows it, and ?status=withdrawn shows the cards Purser closed on its own; GET /suggestions/counts says how many of each kind are open (snoozed ones left out), and GET /suggestions/{id} adds the full evidence. A match card shows the expected row against the bank row and the variance, with Accept, Snooze and Reject. A transfer pair card shows where the money left and arrived, both dates and both bank texts, with Link as transfer, Snooze and Not a transfer. Transfer pairs, transfer links and agent proposals carry no confidence, so they sort after everything Purser scored. The Dashboard therefore shows each kind on its own, under its total ("2 transfer pairs to review"), ten cards at a time with Show more for the rest, so no kind is ever hidden behind another. MCP list suggestions (with an optional kind) returns the same rows with a one-line headline, the draft, an evidence summary (count, first/last, amount range, cadence, and an agent's note) and the confidence, beside open (every open row) and open by kind; whats new carries the open count and the top few.

sections.heading: Why it remembers
sections.text: Every suggestion has a stable fingerprint — the account it lives on plus who it is with (a payee, or a counterparty account); for a transfer link, the two accounts in either order plus the payee. One row per fingerprint, ever: a pattern found tomorrow lands on the same row, a pattern you rejected last week stays rejected, and a pattern already covered by one of your schedules — or a pair and payee one of your transfer link rules already covers — is never suggested at all. That is what keeps the inbox from becoming noise. A match's fingerprint is the bill's schedule slot (or the expected row) plus the bank row, so rejecting it holds even when the bill comes back as a fresh copy in the same slot. A transfer pair's fingerprint is its two bank rows, in either order — as they were before any correction, so a correction of either row keeps the same card and the same "not a transfer". A transfer link's payee is matched through its aliases : if a rename rule later merges that payee into a friendlier one, a confirm under the new name still refreshes the same suggestion, and a rejection still holds. The authoritative spec is DESIGN.md section 6 (schedules and forecasting) and decisions 57, 67, 86 and 102. Schedules themselves are covered in Scheduled transactions and recurring bills, rules in Write deterministic rules.

pages.title: Manage transfers
pages.description: How Purser links the two sides of a transfer deterministically, when it asks first, and how to convert, absorb, and unlink.

sections.text: A transfer between your own accounts is not spending. In Purser it is one transaction with two real-account postings — money leaving assets.checking and arriving in assets.savings — not two unrelated rows. Getting the two bank sides joined into that single transaction is what this page is about. A loan payment whose bank sides differ by its interest is the one variation: it adds a single interest/fee posting (see Confirm a split loan payment).

sections.heading: Deterministic auto-linking
sections.text: At import (and on the daily sweep), Purser looks for opposite-amount pairs across accounts whose dates are at most 3 days apart. A pair is auto-linked only when the amount-and-window match is joined by a signal : - a name signal — a transfer or payment-style keyword (transfer, xfer, payment, autopay, ...) or the counterparty account's own name in the text; - a declared pair — an active transfer link rule for the two accounts, which can also give that pair its own window (see Declared pairs and their window); - a scheduled transfer — a transfer schedule's instance covers the pair (see Scheduled transfers below). When a signal is present the two one-sided rows merge into a single transfer and the originals are voided with links back. This is deterministic by design — no scoring, no guessing. Every auto-merge is logged, evented, badged, and reversible : it writes an audit row, emits a transfer.auto linked event whose signal names what linked it — rule:<rule id , name or schedule:<schedule id , the first that applies — shows a badge in the register, and can be undone with unlink. The auto path acts on posted rows only ; pending pairs stay confirm-first until they post. Turn it off entirely with the PURSER TRANSFER AUTO LINK setting (Settings - General, default on) — then every candidate waits for you.

sections.heading: Scheduled transfers
sections.text: A transfer schedule — a monthly savings sweep, a 529 contribution — already says which two accounts move how much, and when. That is enough to link its bank rows, even when their descriptors carry no keyword at all (FID BKG SVC LLC MONEYLINE on one side, MONEY LINE RECEIVED EFT on the other). A pair is covered when an instance of an active transfer schedule: - names the same two accounts, in the same direction; - has exactly the pair's amount — an estimated instance whose amount differs from the bank's is not a signal; link those by name, by rule, or by confirming; - is dated within the 3-day window of both legs. The bank legs of a transfer often post a day or more apart, and the nightly job matches expectations before it links transfers, so the first leg is usually matched to the instance by the time its counterpart arrives — proposed when only the amount and date agree, matched outright when the description agrees too. That leg stays linkable: a bank row matched to an expected transfer still pairs with a row on that transfer's other account (never with anything else), so the pair links whichever side posts first. Either way the instance ends up settled once, by the merged transfer : a confirmed match moves onto the merge, a proposal is replaced by an automatic match on it, and an instance that was still open is matched to the merge at link time. The merged transfer is then matched, so no other expectation can claim it. A bank row matched to an ordinary bill is never pulled into a transfer this way. When an estimated instance is off — the card statement says 8,347.00, not the balance the schedule estimated — override the instance to the statement amount (Rules and instances). Both of its legs move, and an instance at exactly the bank's amount is a signal again, so the payment links when its bank rows arrive.

sections.heading: Confirm-first candidates
sections.text: An amount-and-window pair with no signal is a candidate , not an auto-link: it looks like a transfer but Purser will not merge it silently. A bank row already matched to an expected transfer is still listed with its counterpart, and confirming the pair carries the match onto the transfer. Posted rows pair first, as the auto-linker pairs them; a pending row pairs only with what is left, so it never takes a posted row's counterpart. Positive rows explicitly labeled as refunds, cash-back/reward credits, dividends or earned-interest credits are excluded from this amount-and-date candidate search. A coincidentally equal debit is not evidence that an earned credit moved between your accounts. Explicit confirmation remains available when you have verified that the bank mislabeled a genuine transfer. A bank row the categorize pass categorized after it posted stays a transfer leg: correcting a posted row writes a reversal and a replacement, and the replacement carries the bank line on — it links, absorbs, and gets its card, just as the original would have. A row you (or an agent) categorized by hand stays out of every automatic link: the category you chose is a decision, and only an explicit confirm or [account] edit makes it part of a transfer. Editing only its description or payee is no such decision — the row stays uncategorized and still links. Confirming ids you read before the categorize pass corrected one of them links the replacement. You meet candidates in two places: - The suggestions inbox. After each import and the nightly matching job, a candidate whose two sides have both posted, the newer in the last 60 days , becomes a transfer pair card on the Dashboard (and in MCP list suggestions), and Purser emits one transfer.candidate event for it. A pair with a side still pending waits until both post. Link as transfer merges the pair; Not a transfer remembers that it is not one; snooze hides it for 30 days. See the suggestions inbox. - The register. Every candidate, however old, shows a Link ⇄ button on its rows, and a ✗ beside it for "not a transfer". Over the API the list is GET /matching/transfer-candidates: the whole history by default, or ?lookback days=N for pairs whose newer side is at most N days old. Each pair names its inbox card as suggestion id when it has one. Reading the list changes nothing. To merge a pair yourself, use the card, the register's Link ⇄, or confirm transfer (MCP) / POST /matching/confirm-transfer. Or leave it as two categorized rows.

sections.heading: Not a transfer
sections.text: Rejecting a candidate is remembered, and not only by the inbox. Purser never links that pair automatically again: not by a keyword in the bank text, not by a transfer link rule you activate later (its projected link count leaves the pair out, so the count you confirm is still what gets linked), and not by an AI or rule conversion to [account] — an AI or rule answer that names the other row's account counts as no answer at all, so neither row becomes a transfer to the other's account by automation (the categorize pass leaves the row to its next tier; a rule's apply-history skips it and reports skipped not a transfer). The pair also leaves the candidate list. Each row stays free for its real counterpart, though: if the money actually went to another of your accounts, that pair can still link or become a card. The rejection follows each row through what comes after it — the posted row the bank replaces a pending one with (also while an outage repair or a manual re-fetch has brought the posted row in but no regular sync has retired the pending yet), the replacement a correction writes, and the copy an unlink brings back — so it holds for the same bank lines, and rejecting by the old ids or the new ones is the same rejection. The register's ✗ rejects through the pair's card when it has one. For an older pair with no card, it uses: curl -sX POST https://purser.example.com/matching/transfer-candidates/reject \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $PURSER TOKEN" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"outgoing id": "CHECKING ROW ID", "incoming id": "SAVINGS ROW ID"}' It needs write scope, like deciding a card. Repeating it changes nothing (already rejected: true). To link a rejected pair after all, confirm it explicitly; like an unlink, a rejection binds only the automatic paths.

sections.heading: From a confirm to a rule
sections.text: A confirm merges that one pair and teaches Purser nothing hidden. What it does instead is visible: it proposes a transfer link rule for the two accounts, scoped to the payee on the rows, as a suggestion in the suggestions inbox. The confirm's response carries its suggestion id. Confirm another pair between the same accounts with the same payee, in either direction, and the same suggestion is refreshed, with each pair you confirmed listed as its evidence. Nothing links because of the suggestion until you decide it: - Accept creates the rule as a draft and tells you how many past pairs it would link. Activating it asks you to confirm that count — the same confirmation as any pair rule. Once active, pairs between those accounts where one side carries the payee (or an alias of it) link on their own, past and future. - Edit and accept narrows or widens the draft first: an exact amount, a date window of 0 to 14 days, or a start date. - Reject is remembered: that pair and payee are never proposed again, or, with "never for this pair", that account pair with any payee. - Snooze brings it back after 30 days. Unlinking a pair you confirmed undoes that merge and nothing else. The suggestion stays in the inbox for you to decide, and no rule exists until you accept one, so the next pair from the same payee stays a confirm-first candidate. A split loan payment proposes no rule, since its unequal sides could never link automatically, and neither does a pair whose rows carry no payee: one confirm is not evidence about every transfer between two accounts.

sections.heading: Declared pairs and their window
sections.text: When two of your accounts transfer to each other regularly but the bank text carries no signal, declare the pair with a transfer link rule — or accept the one a confirm proposed. For that pair the name signal is no longer needed, and the rule can also set the pair's own date window with window days (0 to 14 days; 3 when unset). A card autopay whose two sides post 4 days apart links once its pair rule has window days of 4 or more, while every pair you have not declared keeps the 3-day window. A wider window never takes a row from a closer pair already in your ledger: each pass links everything within 3 days first, exactly as it would without the rule, and pairs the declared accounts farther apart only among the rows left without a partner. Activating the rule asks you to confirm how many historical pairs it will link, counted with its window.

sections.heading: Confirm a split loan payment
sections.text: A loan payment rarely shows the same amount on both sides. Checking reports the whole payment leaving; the loan account reports only the principal it was paid down by; the difference is interest or fees. Those two rows never auto-link (every automatic path needs exactly opposite amounts), so confirm them yourself and name the category the difference belongs to: curl -sX POST https://purser.example.com/matching/confirm-transfer \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $PURSER TOKEN" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"outgoing id": "CHECKING ROW ID", "incoming id": "LOAN ROW ID", "remainder category": "expenses.fees.interest"}' Over MCP, call confirm transfer with the same three arguments. With checking at -612.40 and the loan at +540.15, Purser records one transaction: Posting Amount --- --- assets.checking (the bank's cash leg, unchanged) -612.40 liabilities.carloan (the loan's principal leg, unchanged) 540.15 expenses.fees.interest (the remainder) 72.25 It sums to zero by construction, and it never invents a full-payment 612.40 posting on the loan — each bank leg stays exactly what its bank reported. The response, the audit row and the transfer.confirmed event carry the remainder and its remainder category. The rules: - The incoming (principal) amount must be positive and smaller than the outgoing (cash) amount. Equal legs are an ordinary transfer — confirm them without remainder category. A principal larger than the cash, a zero, or a negative leg is refused with a 422 that names the problem. - remainder category must be an expense category, and not expenses.uncategorized. - It needs write scope, and nothing automatic ever does it — no auto-link, absorb, rule or AI path produces a split. - Unlink restores both bank rows exactly as they were, and the interest posting goes with the split. To change the category, unlink and confirm again. In the register the row shows the other account as its [account] value, with a split line under it giving the remainder amount and category. Over the API the row carries is transfer: true, transfer account path, category path (the remainder category) and remainder amount; MCP search transactions rows carry counterparty, category and remainder. Only the shapes Purser writes count as transfers: a row that touches two real accounts and several categories is shown as what it is, not as a transfer.

sections.heading: Convert a row into a transfer
sections.text: In the flat view a transfer's "category" is the other account in Quicken-style brackets, and the same sugar works for writes. Set a row's category to [assets.savings] (via update transaction or a PATCH) to convert it into a transfer to that account. Depending on what already exists on the other side, the conversion absorbs into a matching transfer, merges with a live one-sided counterpart (including one already matched to an expected transfer between the same two accounts — the match moves onto the merge), or converts in place. Set a plain category back to undo it, naming in account the side that keeps the row. A conversion must be the only change in the call, and a transfer carrying linked bank rows must be unlinked first.

sections.heading: Change a transfer's amount
sections.text: An expected or pending transfer takes a new amount in place: send amount with account naming the side it is read from, and both legs move (a schedule instance defaults to its schedule's account). The direction never changes — an amount whose sign would reverse the transfer is refused. A transfer carrying linked bank rows, a split loan payment and a posted transfer are not edited this way: unlink them so their bank rows come back as separate transactions (convert a posted transfer without bank rows back to a category instead).

sections.heading: Absorb and unlink
sections.text: Absorb handles the late-arriving side: when an imported row matches an existing transfer's unbacked side and carries a name signal (or the pair is declared, within the rule's window), it is voided into that transfer instead of duplicating it (a transfer.absorbed event). A side a bank row already accounts for is never absorbed into: the side of a merged bank row, and the own side of a bank row you (or the categorize pass) converted to [account] — so a second, real payment of the same amount from that account stays a row of its own. Unlink undoes a link — the merged transfer splits back into its one-sided originals (with their content hashes moved onto the resurrected rows) and a transfer.unlinked event fires. If the transfer settled an expectation, such as a scheduled transfer's instance, that settlement goes with it: the instance is due again in its slot and the next matching run decides what settles it — it is never brought back as a posted copy. A pair you explicitly unlinked is suppressed from the auto paths only, and from the candidate list; an explicit confirm or convert can always relink it. The resurrected rows are your bank rows again — even one the categorize pass had recategorized — so each can still link with a different counterpart, and a transfer that survives the unlink (one you made with [account]) has its side open again for the bank row that does belong to it, never for the row you unlinked. The authoritative spec is DESIGN.md sections 5 (matching and transfer tiers) and 3.3 (bracket transfers and split loan payments). See Events and webhooks for the transfer events.

pages.title: CLI
pages.description: One image, multiple roles — purser serve, worker, migrate, plus keygen, seed-demo, and guarded admin commands.

sections.text: The purser command is the single entrypoint for every role. All role commands fail fast without a valid PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY , and a wrong-key canary check fails closed before anything serves.

sections.heading: purser serve
sections.text: Apply migrations, then serve the API, the MCP endpoint, the admin SPA, and the in-process job scheduler. The default single-process deployment.

sections.heading: purser worker
sections.text: Run only the scheduled jobs (sync, matching, forecasting, retention). For the optional role split: run serve with PURSER DISABLE SCHEDULER=true alongside one worker — same image, same configuration.

sections.heading: purser migrate
sections.text: Apply database migrations to head and exit. serve and worker migrate on startup, so this exists for init containers and manual control. Every role holds a Postgres advisory lock while it upgrades, so processes that start together (a serve + worker split) take turns instead of racing: the later one waits, logs that it is waiting, then finds the schema already at head.

sections.heading: purser keygen
sections.text: Print a fresh Fernet key for PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY.

sections.heading: purser seed-demo
sections.text: Seed a small realistic demo dataset: a few accounts, two months of synthetic transactions, a transfer pair, one recurring bill and one card-payment transfer schedule — enough to exercise matching, forecasting, and every read tool without a bank connection. Skips silently when the database already holds user data — any real account or any transaction. What the migrations seed (the category tree and the system account equity.securities) does not count. --force seeds anyway and writes a seed.force audit row.

sections.heading: Guarded admin commands
sections.text: Offline remediation. Back up first.

sections.heading: purser admin delete-account
sections.text: purser admin delete-account <path-or-uuid dry-run pre-flight report purser admin delete-account <path-or-uuid --yes execute Hard-delete a duplicate account and free its content hashes for re-import. Dry-run by default; refuses virtual, SimpleFIN-attached, and parent accounts. The append-only raw feed archive is never touched. This is deliberately a CLI, not an API — no token scope can delete an account.

sections.heading: purser admin purge-feed-rows
sections.text: purser admin purge-feed-rows <path-or-uuid dry-run report purser admin purge-feed-rows <path-or-uuid --since 2026-05-01 bounded purser admin purge-feed-rows <path-or-uuid --yes execute purser admin purge-feed-rows <path-or-uuid --include-corrections --yes Hard-delete an account's feed-origin rows (any status) so the archive can re-derive them — the repair half-step for feed data that imported wrong, such as a sign-inverted stream. QIF, manual, and agent rows are never touched; merge-linked transfers unlink first so the counterpart's bank line survives; the raw feed archive stays whole. Dry-run by default. Follow with replay-archive. A feed row that was corrected after import (recategorized by a person, an agent or a rule, or re-booked as a securities trade's cash) is refused: its correction would stay behind beside the row the replay re-lands, and the account would count it twice. The dry run counts such rows and their correction chains, and lists the ones a person or an agent corrected. --include-corrections purges each corrected row together with its whole correction chain; a correction a person made is then lost, so make it again after the replay. A chain that converted the row to a transfer (a leg on another account) is refused either way: convert it back to a category first. A feed row that a securities sale or purchase linked as its cash (see Track holdings by hand) is refused even with --include-corrections: the dry run counts such rows, and --yes exits naming each trade and these steps: 1. Reopen the position if it is closed. 2. If the account's holdings come from the feed, switch it to manual. 3. Reverse the trade, which gives the row its category back. 4. Purge with --include-corrections. 5. Replay the archive. 6. Record the trade again, linking the re-imported row (transaction id).

sections.heading: purser admin replay-archive
sections.text: purser admin replay-archive <connection-uuid plan only purser admin replay-archive <connection-uuid --since 2026-07-01 bounded purser admin replay-archive <connection-uuid --yes execute Re-import a connection's archived payloads, oldest first. Content-hash idempotent: rows already in the ledger skip, purged rows re-land — with feed invert now set on an account, its rows re-land sign-corrected under their original identities. A posted row that a fetch carried more than a week back under a new description, beside an original the ledger holds, skips as re-described, just as the sync skipped it (skipped redescribed in the summary). Commits per fetch, so an interrupted replay keeps its progress and re-running is safe. A replay re-derives transactions only. A loan balance, a feed-mapped asset's reported value and a brokerage's holdings describe the moment each fetch was made, and the live sync already recorded them, so a replay records no valuations, value changes or holdings snapshots.

sections.heading: purser admin purge-retired-rows
sections.text: purser admin purge-retired-rows <path-or-uuid list batches purser admin purge-retired-rows <path-or-uuid --batch <created at dry-run report purser admin purge-retired-rows <path-or-uuid --batch <created at --apply execute Remove import rows that have no source fetch : rows an ingest path that no longer exists left behind, whose archived payloads are gone, so purge-feed-rows — which selects rows by fetch — cannot reach them. Manual QIF and CSV imports have no source fetch either, so the unit of removal is a creation batch : every row one import commits shares that transaction's created at timestamp. Without --batch, the command lists the account's batches, oldest first, each with its row count by status, its date range, and the audit actions recorded at the same instant — qif.import or csv.import marks a manual import. The audit trail is pruned after audit retention days, so an old batch may show none. Name the batch you mean with --batch, copying the timestamp exactly as listed (repeat the flag for several); the dry run then prints the counts and a sample of the rows. --apply (alias --yes) removes the batch by the ledger's own rules: - pending and expected rows are voided through the normal void path and stay as lineage; - posted rows are hard-deleted through the same guarded delete purge-feed-rows uses; - rows already void are left alone. A row with a live link refuses unless you pass --unlink: a proposed match is rejected, a confirmed match is undone (the bill it settled is expected again), and a merged transfer is unlinked — the other account's bank line comes back on its own account while this account's side goes with the batch. A row that was corrected after import, or that posts to another real account, always refuses. The apply run recomputes the plan and refuses if it no longer matches what the dry run showed. Each run is audited and emits account.retired rows purged; the raw feed archive is never touched.

sections.heading: purser admin rotate-key
sections.text: Re-encrypt every encrypted column under a new primary key. Run with both keys configured — PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY="<new ,<old " — and ciphertexts re-wrap without exposing plaintext; blind indexes and content hashes stay byte-identical. Drop the old key afterwards.

pages.title: Configuration
pages.description: Every PURSER_* environment variable, and which settings are runtime-editable in the admin UI.

sections.text: Purser is configured through PURSER environment variables (a .env file next to the process also works). A subset can be overridden at runtime in the admin UI (under Settings : General , Security , Connections , Prices , Categories and Agents & API ) or via the admin-scoped /config REST API; overrides persist in the database and win over the environment.

sections.heading: Required
sections.text: Variable Purpose --- --- PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY Fernet key for data encrypted at rest (raw bank envelopes, SimpleFIN access URLs, webhook secrets, narrative text). Every role command fails fast without it. Accepts comma-separated keys during rotation — the first key encrypts. Generate with purser keygen. Record it: encrypted data is unrecoverable without it.

sections.heading: Environment-only
sections.text: Infrastructure identity — never runtime-editable. Variable Default Purpose --- --- --- PURSER DATABASE URL postgresql+psycopg://purser:purser@localhost:5432/purser PostgreSQL DSN (psycopg v3 driver). PURSER PUBLIC URL http://localhost:8000 External base URL of the instance. Drives cookie security (https:// = secure cookies), the OIDC redirect URI, and the MCP endpoint's Host/Origin allowlist (requests for any other host get HTTP 421). The Helm chart derives it from the ingress host. Serve Purser at the root of its host (https://purser.example.com): a path prefix (https://example.com/purser) is not supported, because the web UI, its icons, the API and /mcp/ all use root-absolute paths. PURSER HOST 0.0.0.0 Bind address. PURSER PORT 8000 Bind port. PURSER LOG LEVEL INFO Log level. PURSER MAX REQUEST BYTES 33554432 (32 MiB) Largest request body accepted. A bigger one is refused with 413 before it is read, signed in or not. 0 turns the limit off; a reverse proxy's own limit applies as well. PURSER DISABLE SCHEDULER false Set on the API process when a dedicated purser worker runs the jobs. The Helm chart sets it on the API pods when worker.enabled=true. PURSER WIDGETS DIR /app/widgets Directory of built MCP Apps widget bundles. PURSER STATIC DIR /app/static Directory of the built web UI (SPA) bundle. Dev falls back to frontend/dist when this has no index.html. PURSER DOCS URL unset Base URL of the deployed docs site. search docs returns absolute links when set, site-relative paths when not. PURSER SOURCE URL https://github.com/mlamoure/purser Where this instance's source code is published. GET /source redirects here, and the web UI footer and /llms.txt point to it. If you run a modified Purser, set it to your own published source (see Licence and notices).

sections.heading: Sign-in throttling
sections.text: Environment-only. Password sign-in (POST /auth/login) counts failures per email and per client address. At a limit, further attempts get 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (seconds) and the password is not checked — see Security model. Counts live in memory, per process. 0 turns a limit off. Variable Default Purpose --- --- --- PURSER LOGIN MAX FAILURES 5 Consecutive failed sign-ins for one email (case-insensitive) before its attempts are refused. A successful sign-in resets it. PURSER LOGIN IP MAX FAILURES 20 Failed sign-ins from one client address, across all emails, before its attempts are refused. A success does not reset it. IPv6 addresses count per /64. PURSER LOGIN BACKOFF SECONDS 30 First lockout. It doubles with each further failure. PURSER LOGIN BACKOFF MAX SECONDS 900 Longest lockout. PURSER LOGIN FAILURE RESET SECONDS 3600 A count is forgotten after this long with no failure and no lockout in force. The client address is the connection's peer as uvicorn reports it. Behind a reverse proxy (Traefik, nginx, an ingress) every request comes from the proxy unless uvicorn is told to believe the proxy's X-Forwarded-For: set uvicorn's own FORWARDED ALLOW IPS variable to the proxy's address or network (default 127.0.0.1,::1), and list nothing else — any address on that list can claim to be any client. Without it, the per-address limit counts the whole instance's failed sign-ins together, so a password spray pauses password sign-in for everyone until the lockout ends. SSO sign-in and agent tokens are unaffected. With Docker Compose, see Put Purser behind a reverse proxy.

sections.heading: Runtime-editable
sections.text: Environment value is the bootstrap default; the admin UI can override each of these live. Secrets (ai api key, oidc client secret, price api key) are write-only and encrypted at rest. Variable Default Purpose --- --- --- PURSER SESSION TTL DAYS 7 Absolute browser-session lifetime. PURSER SESSION IDLE HOURS 8 Sliding idle timeout for browser sessions. PURSER AUDIT RETENTION DAYS 90 Audit call/change rows older than this are pruned nightly (floor 7). PURSER TRANSFER AUTO LINK true Deterministic transfer auto-linking at import. Off = every candidate is confirm-first. PURSER PRIVACY PURCHASE false Agents receive payees as stable references (py ...), with descriptions, memos and bill names left out, unless a call asks for them with include. See Privacy and agents. PURSER PRIVACY AMOUNT false Agents receive no single-transaction or bill amounts unless a call asks for them. Totals and balances stay exact. PURSER AI PROVIDER none AI categorization provider: none, openai (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), or anthropic. PURSER AI BASE URL https://api.openai.com/v1 OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenRouter...). PURSER AI API KEY unset Provider API key (write-only secret). PURSER AI MODEL unset Model name. PURSER AI REVIEW false Run the review pass server-side instead of waiting for a connected agent. Requires a configured provider on top of this — turning a provider on grants nothing by itself. PURSER REVIEW MAX AGE DAYS 90 Unreviewed transactions older than this are auto-marked aged by a nightly sweep, so the set cannot grow without bound. The count is reported rather than cleared silently. PURSER OIDC ISSUER unset OpenID Provider issuer URL (e.g. an Authentik instance). SSO enables when issuer, client id, and secret are all set; password login always remains as fallback. PURSER OIDC CLIENT ID unset OIDC client id. PURSER OIDC CLIENT SECRET unset OIDC client secret (write-only secret). PURSER OIDC AUTO PROVISION false Auto-create a member account for an SSO identity whose email matches no account, ignoring letter case (requires the provider to assert email verified). Off by default: such sign-ins get "account not provisioned" — pre-create users in the admin UI ( Settings - Users ) instead. PURSER GRAFANA URL unset Grafana base URL for deep links on tool responses; links omitted when unset. PURSER PRICE PROVIDER none Daily closes for hand-tracked positions: none (record closes by hand) or tiingo. The provider sees ticker symbols only. See Track holdings by hand. PURSER PRICE STALE DAYS 7 A hand-tracked position whose newest close is older than this many days is flagged stale (and price.stale fires once). 1 to 365. PURSER FEED STALE DAYS 4 A mapped SimpleFIN account whose bank balance date is more than this many days old is stale: feed.stale fires once per frozen date and whats new lists it until the bank updates. 1 to 90. Runtime-editable through PUT /config (feed stale days). See Connect a bank with SimpleFIN. PURSER TIMEZONE UTC The household time zone, an IANA name such as America/New York. Its calendar date is "today" everywhere Purser reasons about days: due and overdue bills, matching's late bills, snoozes, the digest's week ahead, net worth and balance defaults, review age, reconciliation's "no future dates", price and feed staleness, and the Grafana forecast view. Timestamps (audit log, fetches, sessions) are stored in UTC and shown in the household time zone by the admin app; the scheduled job times stay UTC (06:45 matching and the rest), except the daily SimpleFIN sync, whose time ( Settings - Connections ) is a clock time in the household time zone and keeps it across daylight-saving changes; changing the zone keeps that clock time in the new zone. The default keeps an existing install on the day it already had. Runtime-editable through Settings - General or PUT /config (timezone); an unknown zone is refused with 422, and an unknown PURSER TIMEZONE stops startup. Any token with read scope gets the current ledger day and zone from GET /clock, for a client that dates its own writes. The price provider's API key has no environment variable on purpose: Purser is the party that sends it, so it lives only in Purser's encrypted settings ( Settings - Prices , or PUT /config with price api key). It is write-only: responses report only price api key set. The SimpleFIN sync schedule (daily / every 12h / every 6h / hourly) is runtime-only — set it in Settings - Connections .

sections.heading: Compose extras
sections.text: The bundled docker-compose.yml also reads POSTGRES PASSWORD (defaults to purser) for the sidecar database. Set it before the first start; see Run with Docker Compose.

sections.heading: Docker host binding
sections.text: The Compose file uses PURSER BIND ADDRESS (default 127.0.0.1) for its published host port. This is a Compose setting, not an application setting. Complete first-admin setup before exposing a remote interface. Compose also passes PURSER PUBLIC URL through to the application; use your HTTPS URL behind a reverse proxy (see Put Purser behind a reverse proxy).

pages.title: Events and webhooks
pages.description: The durable event stream, every event type, and HMAC-signed webhook delivery.

sections.text: Every notable state change appends a row to a durable events stream in the same transaction as the change itself. Consume it two ways: poll GET /events (read scope, cursor-paginated — the same stream the whats new MCP tool digests), or register webhooks.

sections.heading: Event types
sections.text: Type Fires when --- --- account.closed An account is closed: its leftover balance posted (to an adjustment category, or for a hand-valued asset as its last change in value against equity.revaluation) and its feed unmapped. account.deleted A duplicate account is hard-deleted via the guarded CLI. account.feed rows purged An account's feed-origin rows are hard-deleted via the guarded purge-feed-rows CLI. account.moved An account moves to a new path (PATCH /accounts/{id} with path). The payload carries the new path, the from path, and accounts moved — the account plus every account beneath it. account.reconciled An account is reconciled to a statement balance (adjustment posted when needed, claim recorded). Payload below. account.reopened A closed account is reopened. account.retired rows purged Import rows with no source fetch are removed by creation batch via the guarded purge-retired-rows CLI; the payload names the batches and counts transactions voided and transactions deleted. balance.drift A synced account's feed-reported balance disagrees with the ledger (once per drift episode; cash and card accounts, plus a hand-tracked brokerage account whose feed balance an admin marked as its cash); the payload's mode names the basis the delta is measured on, posted only or pending inclusive, and basis pinned: true appears only when that basis is the account's admin-set pin rather than learned. bill.late An expected transaction (a schedule instance, a manual bill, or an uncleared imported row) passes its date unmatched. feed.account failed A mapped SimpleFIN account reports an account-level error (act.failed, act.missingdata) on two syncs in a row. Once per episode: the payload carries account (the path), institution, code and message. Usually clears on its own; feed.recovered follows the first clean sync. feed.auth required A SimpleFIN bank login reports a connection-level error (con.auth: log in to that bank again in SimpleFIN Bridge). Once per episode, from the first sync that reports it: the payload carries institution (the login's name), conn id, code and message. feed.recovered A feed problem clears. The payload's kind says which: auth (with institution, conn id), account failed (with account, institution) or stale (with account, institution, the new balance date and stale since, the frozen date). feed.stale A mapped SimpleFIN account's bank balance date is more than feed stale days (default 4) days old: the bank has stopped updating, often because its login needs attention. Once per account and frozen date, so a bank that updates and freezes again fires again: the payload carries account, institution, balance date and stale days (its age). forecast.shortfall The nightly forecast scan (07:15 UTC) projects an account that has a floor (min balance) below that floor within the next 30 days. Accounts without a floor are not scanned, even when projected below zero, and a forecast balance call never emits it. The floor is set at creation or later through PATCH /accounts/{id}, MCP update account or the app (write scope); the next scan uses the change, and clearing it stops the event. Once per account and first shortfall date: the payload carries account (the path), date (the first day below the floor), low (the 30-day projected minimum) and min balance. match.proposed The matcher proposes an expected-vs-imported pair. match.confirmed A match is confirmed. pending.vanished A pending imported transaction disappears from the feed with no posted successor (none of the same amount on its account within 7 days), and is voided. whats new counts these. position.updated A hand-tracked position changes: opened, renamed, an event recorded or reversed, closed, or reopened, or one of its lots voided or its basis corrected. The payload names the account path, position id, symbol and change (opened, renamed, recorded, reversed, closed, reopened, lot voided, lot basis); a rename adds the new name (null when cleared), a recorded or reversed event adds kind, occurred on and quantity held (today's share count), a recorded trade that moved cash adds its cash row's cash transaction id, and a lot change adds lot id. holdings.captured A lot or award capture is applied (Track tax lots and equity awards). The payload carries account (the path), kind (lots or awards), as of, completeness, changes (counts by kind), repeat (the same holdings as the previous capture: freshness only) and, for lots, symbols and skipped symbols. An exact retry of an applied capture emits nothing. Never a lot or grant reference. award.updated An equity award changes: a vest recorded (change vested, with vest date, net quantity and linked), a vest forfeited or set back to scheduled (forfeited, scheduled), or its units corrected (updated). The payload carries award id and symbol, never the grant reference. price.fetch failed The price fetch (daily, or an admin's fetch-now) could not get or store some of a symbol's closes: the provider refused or failed a request, the store failed, or the answer carried closes out of range, which are dropped. Once per symbol per day for a failed request, and once more that day when closes were dropped, however often the fetch runs; the payload carries provider, symbol, status (the HTTP status, 200 for dropped closes, or null for a transport or store failure) and reason (a fixed phrase such as refused or 2 close(s) out of range dropped, or an exception's class name). Never the API key or a provider message. price.stale A symbol held by a hand-tracked position has a newest close older than the staleness threshold, or no close at all. Once per symbol per stale close: the payload's price as of (null when there is none) and stale days; a fresher close ends it, and a later stale close fires again. holding.unpriced A brokerage feed reports a held fund with no value (0 or none: a plan-only fund no provider prices) and no recorded price values it. Once per account and symbol when it turns unpriced, re-armed once the position was priced: the payload carries account (the path), symbol, quantity, as of (the date of the set it sits in) and unpriceable. record price under the fund's ticker values it; when unpriceable is true the feed sent a description instead of a ticker, and no recorded price can value it. holding.period open A brokerage account switched back to the feed still counts its hand-tracked holdings because no sync of it has arrived since, for longer than the price staleness threshold. Once per account and switch: the payload carries account (the path), since (the day of the switch) and stale days. Check the connection, or the account's mapping. recurring.price changed A recurring charge posts at a new amount. suggestion.created A new suggestion lands in the inbox (detected pattern, agent proposal, new-liability scan, a manual transfer confirm proposing a transfer link rule, a match proposal's card — emitted beside match.proposed — or a transfer candidate's card, emitted beside transfer.candidate); dedup key is its fingerprint. The payload carries kind and source; a transfer link one also names account, counterparty account and payee, a match one account, label, expected date and posted amount, a transfer pair one account (where the money left), counterparty account (where it arrived) and amount. A repeat confirm or re-detection refreshes the open suggestion and emits nothing, and so does a card re-opened because its match was proposed again or its pair is a candidate again. "Not a transfer" on a pair that had no card writes its suggestion rejected, and emits this event and suggestion.decided. suggestion.decided A suggestion is accepted, rejected or snoozed; the payload names the kind, the decision and, for accepts, what was created: result entity type schedule (active), rule (a transfer link rule, still a draft until you activate it), match, or transaction (a transfer pair's merged transfer). A match card decided in the register (confirm, reject, or marking the bill paid with that row) emits it too, and so does a transfer pair confirmed or marked "not a transfer" in the register; a card Purser withdraws emits nothing. sync.failed A SimpleFIN sync attempt fails. transaction.posted A transaction reaches posted. transfer.candidate An amount+window pair looks like a transfer but carries no signal (name, transfer link rule or transfer schedule). Emitted once per pair (dedup key = the pair key of the two posted rows as they were before any correction) by the matching pass that runs after each import and in the nightly job, when both sides are posted and the newer is at most 60 days old — the pairs that get an inbox card; reading GET /matching/transfer-candidates emits nothing. Once per pair of bank lines: a later correction of either row, or the posted row that replaces a pending one, does not emit it again. A pair rejected as not a transfer, or unlinked, emits nothing. transfer.auto linked The deterministic auto-linker merges a pair: exact opposite amounts within the window, plus a signal — a name signal, a transfer link rule declaring the pair (whose window days may set that pair's window, and whose payee scope, when it has one, a leg's payee must match), or a transfer schedule's instance covering it. The payload's signal names the first that applies: rule:<rule id , name or schedule:<schedule id . transfer.converted A row became a transfer through the [account] sugar — your edit, a categorize rule or the categorize pass — without merging with another row: converted in place (a pending row) or replaced by a transfer (a posted row). The payload names the transfer id, the account the row was on and the counterparty account; dedup key is the id of the account the row was on. An [account] edit that merges two rows or absorbs one emits transfer.confirmed or transfer.absorbed instead. transfer.confirmed A transfer pair is merged by an explicit confirm. A split loan payment's payload also carries remainder (the interest/fee amount) and remainder category; those keys are absent on an ordinary transfer. transfer.absorbed A late-arriving counterpart is absorbed into an existing transfer. transfer.unlinked A transfer link is undone. valuation.recorded A loan valuation is recorded. asset.stale A hand-valued asset's value is older than its revalue after days (the daily check at 07:20 UTC). Once per stale value: payload account (path), last valued (null when never valued), revalue after days. whats new lists such assets in stale assets on every call until a value is recorded. asset.value changed A hand-valued asset's value changed: a value change recorded or reversed, or a feed-reported balance applied. Payload: account id, path, as of, amount (signed), transaction id, and reference or reverses. A value set by reconciling emits account.reconciled instead. variance.threshold A matched pair's amount variance exceeds the threshold.

sections.heading: account.reconciled payload
sections.text: Emitted once, when a reconciliation is recorded. Dry runs and retries emit nothing. The event's entity id is the account. Amounts are decimal strings in the ledger's sign (a card is negative when owed), except statement balance, which is the figure as the statement prints it: { "path": "liabilities.card", "currency": "USD", "reconciliation id": "8d1f6c0e-5b7a-4f0e-9c3d-2a6b1e4f7c90", "as of": "2026-09-30", "basis": "posted", "component": "balance", "statement balance": "425.0000", "target balance": "-425.0000", "ledger balance": "-400.0000", "adjustment": "-25.0000", "adjustment tx id": "c4a2e9b1-7d3f-4e86-b5a0-91f2d6c8e3b7" } component is cash for a manual brokerage cash reconciliation and balance for ordinary cash/card accounts. It never claims that brokerage securities were reconciled. ledger balance is the balance on as of in that basis before the adjustment. adjustment is "0.0000" and adjustment tx id is null for a clean reconcile. A reconciliation that later goes out of balance emits no event; reads report it. See Reconcile an account.

sections.heading: Webhooks
sections.text: Manage subscriptions with admin scope: - POST /webhooks — subscribe a URL to event types (wildcards supported); an optional per-subscription secret is encrypted at rest. A new subscription receives events from its creation onward — for history, replay GET /events instead. - GET /webhooks, DELETE /webhooks/{id} — list and remove. - GET /webhooks/{id}/deliveries — delivery log with response codes. - POST /webhooks/deliver — process due deliveries immediately (the worker also does this on schedule).

sections.heading: Delivery contract
sections.text: Each delivery is an HTTP POST of the event JSON with: Header Content --- --- X-Purser-Event The event type. X-Purser-Delivery Unique delivery id (dedupe on this). X-Purser-Signature Hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with the subscription secret. Only when a secret is set. Verify by recomputing the HMAC over the raw request body . Non-2xx responses retry with exponential backoff — 1, 4, 16, and 64 minutes — then the delivery is marked failed after 5 attempts. Replay missed events any time from GET /events with your last cursor.

sections.heading: account_balance
sections.text: Point-in-time balance of one real account (UUID or path). Open loan accounts answer with their latest valuation at or before as of (method 'valuation'); open brokerage accounts add their latest holdings market value on top of the postings basis (method 'postings+holdings'); everything else answers from the STORED running balances alone (method 'postings'; register semantics: chain-head pending+posted rows). as of is an ISO date, default today; 0 before the account's first activity; closed accounts answer their whole history. bank snapshot carries the latest bank-reported and available balances, their currency, source timestamp/precision, ingestion time and freshness, under the same read scope. Available balance is separate (e.g. remaining credit on a card). Its comparison reports live posted and pending-inclusive totals over ALL recorded dates, the effective/learned/pinned basis and exact bank-minus-ledger difference; matches either basis is the separate alert policy. Null means unknown/unavailable, never zero. Even with as of, this snapshot is LATEST, not historical bank truth. For a balance over TIME, call balance history instead of looping this. Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- account string yes — as of string \ null no null

sections.heading: archive_memory
