sections.heading: skip_instance
sections.text: Skip one occurrence of a schedule (write scope): the expected instance is voided and its slot stays filled, so it does not come back — use it for "not this month". The schedule itself is untouched. Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- transaction id string yes —

sections.heading: spending_summary
sections.text: Server-side spending aggregation — no row paging, no client-side arithmetic. Classic mode groups by category payee month over an optional date range. Baseline mode (period='YYYY-MM' + baseline = avg 3mo avg 12mo same month last year) answers 'where did my money go vs my usual?': per-row amount/baseline/delta with top payee mover attribution; when period is the current month the baseline is pace-adjusted to like days elapsed. Drill a category with (category=..., group by='payee', period, baseline) — same signature, payee rows. grand total/baseline total sum ALL matching spending even when rows truncate. Totals are positive-for-spend (category-leg convention); search transactions amounts are negative-for-spend. Renders as the spending widget in MCP Apps hosts. include: fields to return although the user's privacy defaults withhold them — any of payee, description, amount, external ids. Ask only for what the user's question needs; a response names what it withheld in withheld. Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- group by string no "category" start string \ null no null end string \ null no null category string \ null no null period string \ null no null baseline string \ null no null include array of string \ null no null

sections.heading: trigger_sync
sections.text: Fetch from SimpleFIN now (archive-first, then import). Omit connection id to sync every active connection. Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- connection id string \ null no null

sections.heading: update_account
sections.text: Rename, re-describe or hide a real account, or set its floor (write scope); only the fields sent change. asset kind sets what a hand-valued asset (type property) is: house, land, car, boat, rv, jewelry, art, equipment or other (a label and an icon only). secured by, on a loan, names the hand-valued asset that secures it (its path or id; "" clears it), so the asset reports its equity. revalue after days, on an asset, is how many days its value may go without an update before Purser calls it stale (asset.stale, whats new.stale assets); 0 turns that off. name is the display name only: the account's path, which tools, rules and outside integrations use to find it, never changes, so a rename breaks nothing that refers to the account. The name is also what transfer auto-link looks for in bank text (a row that mentions the counterparty account's name is a transfer signal), so a rename changes which bank descriptions link to the account. description="" clears it. hidden=true hides the account in the app's account list only: it still syncs, counts in net worth, and is listed by list accounts with hidden=true. min balance is the account's floor, a decimal string in ledger sign: use it when the user says "warn me if checking goes under $500" (min balance="500.00"). Each night Purser projects the next 30 days and emits a forecast.shortfall event when the projection drops below the floor; forecast balance shows it as min balance. A credit card is negative when owed, so "warn me past $4,500 owed" is "-4500.00". min balance="" clears the floor and stops the warnings. Checking, savings, cash and credit-card accounts only. Categories are renamed in the app, not here, and moving an account to another path is done in the app too. Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- account string yes — name string \ null no null description string \ null no null hidden boolean \ null no null min balance string \ null no null asset kind string \ null no null secured by string \ null no null revalue after days integer \ null no null

sections.heading: update_award_vest
sections.text: Forfeit a scheduled vest (status 'forfeited'), reinstate a forfeited one, or set a vest that was LINKED to an existing lot back to 'scheduled' (write scope). A vest recorded as an event goes back by reversing that event (reverse position event). vest id comes from list awards(award=...). Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- vest id string yes — status string yes — note string \ null no null

sections.heading: update_occurrence_certainty
sections.text: Set evidence on just this occurrence's amount and/or date. Address it by transaction id, or by schedule id plus occurrence date (works for a projected slot beyond the materialized window: the rule's amount and date stay, the evidence moves onto the instance when it materializes). Each supplied dimension needs state (estimated/confirmed), source, as of and a note; value is optional (omit to keep the current value; a schedule-slot address accepts only its current value). A fixed amount is a model, not proof: mark it estimated without changing it. History is an estimate, never confirmation evidence. Confirm only what the supplied statement, paystub, invoice or user instruction establishes; omit the other dimension. clear returns a dimension to the rule's certainty. This never posts cash or confirms later occurrences. Link a real posted payment with match instead; ambiguous candidates require review. Original estimates and superseded confirmations remain available in Purser. include: fields to return although the user's privacy defaults withhold them — any of payee, description, amount, external ids. Ask only for what the user's question needs; a response names what it withheld in withheld. Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- transaction id string \ null no null amount object \ null no null date object \ null no null schedule id string \ null no null occurrence date string \ null no null clear array of string \ null no null include array of string \ null no null

sections.heading: update_schedule
sections.text: Edit a schedule's rule (write scope); only the fields sent change ("" clears payee or memo; a flat schedule keeps at least one). Live instances the user has not overridden follow the new rule (slots the rule no longer produces are dropped, amounts re-estimated, missing slots added); overridden ("pinned") instances keep their amounts and dates. A new payee or memo relabels every live instance, pinned ones too, whose description or payee still equals the old one (relabeled counts them); labels set by hand stay. category and counterparty account are mutually exclusive: sending one switches the schedule's shape between flat and transfer. Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- schedule id string yes — name string \ null no null rrule string \ null no null dtstart string \ null no null amount string \ null no null amount type string \ null no null date mode string \ null no null estimate basis string \ null no null payee string \ null no null memo string \ null no null category string \ null no null autopost policy string \ null no null counterparty account string \ null no null

sections.heading: update_transaction
sections.text: Edit a transaction. pending/expected edit in place; posted becomes an atomic reversal+replacement pair. Transfers ride the category field: category='[account path]' converts the row into a transfer to that account (absorbing or merging with the bank row on the other side when one exists). To turn a transfer back into a categorized row, send a plain category plus account='the side that keeps the row'. Conversions must be the only change in the call. An amount on an expected/pending transfer is the leg of account (a schedule instance defaults to its schedule's account), keeps that leg's sign and moves both legs; a posted or bank-linked transfer is refused, and the error says how to correct it. On a schedule instance an amount, date or category edit pins it (the rule stops re-estimating it; undo with reset instance); a description or payee edit is a label and does not. Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- transaction id string yes — amount string \ null no null category string \ null no null payee string \ null no null description string \ null no null account string \ null no null

sections.heading: upsert_awards
sections.text: Bulk, idempotent input of equity awards and their vest schedules (write scope): awards [{grant ref (the broker's grant id: the award's identity), symbol, granted on, granted quantity, cancelled quantity, vested quantity (as the broker reports it), plan, schedule: [{vest date, quantity, ordinal (only for two vests on one date)}] — the vests not yet delivered}]. Same contract as upsert lots: dry run=true by default, commit with expect hash, exact retries are no-ops, conflicts are never applied. Awards never touch holdings or net worth: a vest becomes shares only through record vest. A re-estimated scheduled quantity, new vests, more cancelled units and a new reported vested count are applied; a changed grant size, fewer cancelled units, or (complete) a scheduled future vest the broker no longer lists is a conflict — forfeit it with update award vest if it is gone. A scheduled vest on or before as of that the broker no longer lists is counted as due: record it. Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- account string yes — as of string yes — completeness string yes — awards array of object yes — captured at string yes — source note string \ null no null dry run boolean no true expect hash string \ null no null skip conflicts boolean no false

sections.heading: upsert_lots
sections.text: Bulk, idempotent input of a broker's tax lots as of a day (write scope) on a hand-tracked brokerage account. positions: [{symbol, lots: [{acquired on, quantity (shares REMAINING on as of), external ref (the broker's lot reference, when shown: the lot's identity), plan, ordinal (when lots of one date and plan have no reference: 1, 2, ... in a stable order), basis per share and/or cost basis (of the remaining shares; omit when unknown — never 0), acquisition (buy, rsu vest, plan purchase, espp purchase, transfer in, drip, gift, unknown)}]}]. Decimal strings; dates YYYY-MM-DD. completeness: complete (each listed symbol's list is the broker's whole list) or partial (only these rows; nothing is inferred from what is missing). captured at: when you read the page (ISO instant with zone; send the same value on the commit); source note: where (no personal data). dry run=true (the default) returns the plan and plan hash, writing nothing; commit with dry run=false and expect hash=plan hash (refused with preview stale if anything changed). Re-sending the exact same request is a no-op (retry); the same holdings read again later only record freshness. New lots are adopted; a complete capture recounts the position up to the broker's total. Never applied, always conflicts: a lot with fewer remaining shares (record the sale or transfer out naming that lot first), more shares, a lot missing from a complete list, a differing basis (basis policy='replace' takes the broker's when nothing drew on the lot), an ambiguous identity, a partial capture whose new lots exceed the unallocated shares, or a capture older than one applied. skip conflicts=true applies the symbols without any. Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- account string yes — as of string yes — completeness string yes — positions array of object yes — captured at string yes — source note string \ null no null basis policy string no "keep" dry run boolean no true expect hash string \ null no null skip conflicts boolean no false

sections.heading: void_lot
sections.text: Void a lot that a capture adopted wrongly (write scope): it stops counting and stays as read-only history. Refused while a sale or transfer out draws on it (reverse those first with reverse position event, then record them again against the right lots), while an award vest is linked to it, and for a lot opened by an event (reverse that event instead). Then capture again (a new captured at: the exact same request is a no-op) to record the right lot. Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- lot id string yes — note string \ null no null

sections.heading: whats_new
sections.text: The morning brief: everything material since your last call in one compact payload — new transactions (count/total, notable items above the materiality threshold, default $50), confirmed bill matches (variance breaches always itemized), subscription price changes, projected shortfalls, bank-reported balance drift against the ledger (each line names its basis: posted only when that bank's balance leaves pending charges out, else pending inclusive; pinned: true when an admin pinned that basis instead of it being learned), pending transactions the bank dropped without posting (counted; those above the threshold itemized — a dropped refund is money to chase), manually tracked symbols whose price turned stale or that have none (stale prices; record price fixes one), feed positions the feed sends with no value that no recorded close prices (unpriced holdings; record price under the ticker values one, except one marked unpriceable: its feed symbol is no ticker, so no close can value it), brokerage accounts switched back to the feed whose hand-tracked set still counts because no fetch has arrived since (open manual periods: check the connection or the account mapping), the week's expected bills, sync failures, and bank feed problems open now (feed: logins that need the user to log in again at the bank, accounts the bank fails to deliver, accounts whose bank balance has stopped updating; repeated on every call until fixed). Pass the returned cursor on your next call to get only new material; a first call without a cursor looks back 7 days. Every line carries its entity id so you can drill without a search. Narrate this in your own voice; the digest widget is the visual receipt. include: fields to return although the user's privacy defaults withhold them — any of payee, description, amount, external ids. Ask only for what the user's question needs; a response names what it withheld in withheld. Parameter Type Required Default --- --- --- --- since cursor string \ null no null materiality string \ null no null include array of string \ null no null

pages.title: Set up Purser with your AI
pages.description: Step-by-step instructions an AI agent follows to take an empty Docker host to a running Purser with itself connected over MCP.

sections.text: This page is written for an AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, an OpenClaw agent or any other agent that can run shell commands). A person can hand it over with one sentence: Set up Purser for me by following https://mlamoure.github.io/purser/tutorials/ai-setup/ People who prefer to install by hand can follow the Quickstart instead; it covers the same steps.

sections.heading: Instructions for the agent
sections.text: You are installing Purser, a self-hosted personal-finance backend, on a Docker host and connecting yourself to it over MCP. Follow the steps in order. You need no prior knowledge of Purser. Ground rules: - The encryption key is never yours. Generate it straight into a file, never print it, never paste it into chat, never store it in your memory or notes. The human copies it into their password manager. - Some steps are human-only. Each is marked Handoff , with the words to say. Stop there and wait for the human to confirm before you continue. - Never ask for a SimpleFIN setup token in chat. The human pastes it into Purser's own pages. - Stop and report instead of improvising when a check fails. The troubleshooting table lists the known failures. Never delete a Docker volume to "start fresh": it may hold someone's books. Run every command on the Docker host. If you reach the host over SSH, run them there and read the notes in Remote access.

sections.heading: 1. Check the prerequisites
sections.text: Run these and compare the results: docker version --format '{{.Server.Os}}/{{.Server.Arch}}' docker compose version curl --version head -n 1 curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8000/ docker volume ls --filter name=purser-pgdata --format '{{.Name}}' Check Expected If not --- --- --- Docker server platform linux/amd64 or linux/arm64 Stop. The image is published for these two only. On an Apple Silicon Mac, Docker Desktop and Colima report linux/arm64; see Docker on macOS. Compose Docker Compose version v2 or later Ask the human to install or update Docker Compose. curl any version Install curl, or ask the human to. Port 8000 000 (nothing answers) Something already listens on port 8000. See the troubleshooting table. Existing volume no output An earlier Purser install (or an earlier attempt at these steps) exists. Stop and ask the human; an existing database needs its original encryption key, not a new one. You do not need Git, Python, Node or a database on the host, and nothing is built: Docker pulls the published Purser image and PostgreSQL 16 and runs them in containers.

sections.heading: 2. Download the compose file
sections.text: Make a directory for this installation and download the release's compose file into it: mkdir purser && cd purser curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlamoure/purser/v2026.11.3/docker-compose.yml grep -c 'image: ghcr.io/mlamoure/purser:v2026.11.3' docker-compose.yml If mkdir reports that purser already exists, stop and ask the human: it may hold an earlier installation and its key. The last command must print 1. Every later command runs in this purser directory. This page installs the latest release, 2026.11.3. Each release has its own compose file at the same address under its own tag (vYYYY.M.PATCH), and that file names the matching image, here ghcr.io/mlamoure/purser:v2026.11.3, published for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.

sections.heading: 3. Pull the images
sections.text: PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY=keygen docker compose pull This downloads the Purser image for the host's architecture and PostgreSQL 16. keygen is a placeholder that satisfies Compose for utility commands; it is not a key and never starts the application.

sections.heading: 4. Generate the encryption key
sections.text: Write a new key straight into .env, which Compose reads automatically. The key never appears in your output: if [ -e .env ]; then echo "STOP: .env already exists" else (umask 077; PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY=keygen docker compose run --rm --no-deps -T purser keygen \ sed 's/^/PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY=/' .env) fi grep -cE '^PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY=[A-Za-z0-9 -]{43}=$' .env If it prints STOP, the file was left untouched: ask the human before going on. The last command must print 1 (one valid key). Do not cat the file. Handoff: store the key. Say to the human: I generated Purser's encryption key and saved it in the file .env in the purser folder on this machine, without displaying it. Please open that file, copy the value after PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY= into your password manager, and keep it apart from any backups. Purser cannot decrypt your data without it. Tell me when it is stored. I will not read it or keep a copy. Wait for the confirmation. The .env file stays in place (readable only by its owner) so that Docker can restart and upgrade Purser. If the human would rather not keep the key on disk, they can delete .env after step 5 and export PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY themselves before any later docker compose up.

sections.heading: 5. Start Purser
sections.text: docker compose up -d for i in $(seq 1 30); do curl -fs http://localhost:8000/healthz && break; sleep 2; done Expected: {"status":"ok","database":"ok"}. Two containers run, purser and postgres. Migrations apply automatically at startup. Then confirm that setup is still open: curl -s http://localhost:8000/auth/setup/status Expected: {"setup needed":true}.

sections.heading: 6. Handoff: the first-run wizard
sections.text: Only the human can create the administrator and mint your token. Say: Purser is running. Please open http://localhost:8000 in your browser and work through the setup wizard: 1. Create admin : your email and a password of at least 8 characters. 2. Record encryption key : the wizard shows the key Purser is running with, until you acknowledge it. Check that it matches the one you just stored, tick the box, and continue. 3. Connect SimpleFIN (optional, for live bank data): paste a setup token from your SimpleFIN Bridge account, then map the accounts it finds. Paste it only into Purser, never into this chat. You can also skip this. 4. Import history (optional): you can skip it. 5. Connect agent : keep the name agent, click Create agent token , and give me the token it shows. It has read + write access: I act for you, every write I make is recorded in the audit log and can be reversed, and I can never grant myself more access. If the page reloads partway through, sign in: the Dashboard's Finish setting up card links to each step still open. Tell me when you are done, and paste the token here. If the human skipped the last step, they can mint the token later on the Settings - Agents & API page: name it, keep the read and write boxes ticked (the default), leave admin unticked, and click Create token . The token is shown exactly once. When you have the token, check that the wizard finished: curl -s http://localhost:8000/auth/setup/status Expected: {"setup needed":false}. The token is your credential. Keep it only in your MCP client configuration (an environment variable such as PURSER TOKEN where your client supports one) and never write it into logs, notes or files the human did not ask for.

sections.heading: 7. Register the MCP server
sections.text: Purser speaks MCP over streamable HTTP: - Endpoint: http://localhost:8000/mcp on the Docker host. Use the HTTPS URL instead when Purser is published remotely. - Auth header: Authorization: Bearer followed by the token. Pick the snippet for your own client. Each one assumes the token is in the environment variable PURSER TOKEN of the shell you run it from. Claude Code : claude mcp add --transport http purser http://localhost:8000/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $PURSER TOKEN" Codex (CLI, desktop app and IDE extension share ~/.codex/config.toml). Add this table; Codex reads the token from PURSER TOKEN at startup: [mcp servers.purser] url = "http://localhost:8000/mcp" bearer token env var = "PURSER TOKEN" PURSER TOKEN must then be set wherever Codex starts, in every future session. If your sessions have no persistent environment (a CLI agent launched fresh each time, or a GUI app that does not read your shell profile), put the header in the file instead and make the file readable only by its owner: [mcp servers.purser] url = "http://localhost:8000/mcp" http headers = { Authorization = "Bearer YOUR TOKEN" } chmod 600 ~/.codex/config.toml Check the result with codex mcp list. OpenClaw, Gemini and any other MCP client : use the matching recipe in Connect an agent (OpenClaw, Gemini, any other client). Most clients load new servers only in a new session; restart or reload yours if the Purser tools do not appear.

sections.heading: 8. Verify the connection
sections.text: 1. Call describe first. Check that your scopes is ["read", "write"]. describe is the first call of every future session too: it returns the data model, conventions, category tree and accounts in one round-trip. 2. Call list accounts. It succeeds even on an empty instance. If your client cannot load the server yet, check the endpoint directly. The trailing slash matters for curl: /mcp answers with a redirect to /mcp/. curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/mcp/ \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $PURSER TOKEN" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"describe","arguments":{}}}' A reply containing your scopes means the token and endpoint work. Then tell the human what you did, which URL Purser answers on, and that their encryption key and admin password are the two secrets only they hold.

sections.heading: 9. Optional next steps
sections.text: - Live bank data : if SimpleFIN was skipped, the human connects it later under Settings , then Connections , by pasting a setup token there. Details: Connect banks with SimpleFIN. Call trigger sync only when the human wants fresh data; SimpleFIN Bridge allows 24 fetches a day. - Older history : the human uploads a QIF or CSV export on the Import page. See Import QIF and CSV. - Backups : set them up before the books matter. See Backup and restore.

sections.heading: Verify it worked
sections.text: - [ ] curl http://localhost:8000/healthz returns {"status":"ok","database":"ok"}. - [ ] docker compose ps shows purser and postgres running, purser healthy. - [ ] /auth/setup/status returns {"setup needed":false}. - [ ] The human confirmed the encryption key is in their password manager. - [ ] describe returns your scopes of ["read", "write"]. - [ ] list accounts answers without an error. - [ ] The key and the token appear nowhere in your chat output or notes.

sections.heading: Build from source instead
sections.text: The steps above run the published image. Contributors, and anyone who wants to run code from the repository, build the image from a clone instead (this needs Git; the first build takes several minutes): git clone https://github.com/mlamoure/purser.git cd purser PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY=keygen docker compose build purser Then continue with step 4 in the purser clone, where Git ignores .env. The local build takes the image name from the compose file, so it stands in for that release's published image until docker compose pull purser fetches the published one again.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text: Read the application log with docker compose logs purser --tail 50. Symptom Cause Fix --- --- --- docker compose pull fails with failed to resolve reference, TLS handshake timeout, no such host or i/o timeout The host cannot reach the image registry (ghcr.io): no network, a firewall, or a proxy Docker does not use. Check that curl -sI https://ghcr.io/v2/ answers; ask the human to fix the network or configure Docker's proxy, then repeat step 3. A failed pull also prints Some service image(s) must be built from source: ignore that hint, it needs a source clone. docker compose pull fails with manifest unknown or not found The compose file names a tag that does not exist, usually after an edited or partial download. Download the compose file again (step 2); do not edit its image line. docker compose pull or up fails with no matching manifest for a platform, or a container exits with exec format error The Docker server is not linux/amd64 or linux/arm64, or Docker is told to use another platform (DOCKER DEFAULT PLATFORM). Stop. Check step 1's platform and unset DOCKER DEFAULT PLATFORM. Other architectures are unsupported. docker compose up or run starts a build and fails with failed to read dockerfile or unable to prepare context The image was never pulled, so Compose fell back to the file's build: section, which needs a source clone. Run step 3 and fix the error it reports. Never build in this directory. docker compose fails with required variable PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY is missing a value No key in .env or the environment. Repeat step 4, or have the human export the key they stored. The log shows PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY is not a valid Fernet key and the container restarts The value is truncated or not a Purser key. Have the human compare .env with the stored key. The log shows PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY does not match this database with two fingerprints The database volume was created with a different key, usually an earlier install. Stop. Ask the human for the original key. Never delete the volume to get past this. docker compose up fails with port is already allocated or address already in use Another program uses host port 8000. Ask the human to stop it, or publish another port with a docker-compose.override.yml containing ports: !override and the new mapping, plus the matching PURSER PUBLIC URL. /healthz gets no answer The app is still starting or exited. Wait for the loop in step 5; then check docker compose ps and the log. /healthz returns HTTP 503 with {"status":"error","database":"down"} Purser cannot reach PostgreSQL. Check docker compose ps postgres and docker compose logs postgres. /auth/setup/status stays {"setup needed":true} The human has not created the admin yet. Wait for the handoff in step 6. /mcp returns 401 {"error":"invalid or missing bearer token"} The token is missing, mistyped, revoked or expired, or the header lacks the word Bearer. Check the header format; ask the human for a new token from Settings - Agents & API if needed. /mcp returns 421 Misdirected Request The request's host is not localhost or the host in PURSER PUBLIC URL. Set PURSER PUBLIC URL to the URL clients use, then run docker compose up -d again. curl to /mcp returns 307 The bare path redirects to /mcp/. Use /mcp/ with curl; MCP clients follow the redirect. A write tool is refused for scope The token lacks write. Ask the human for a read + write token.

sections.heading: Remote access
sections.text: Compose publishes Purser on 127.0.0.1:8000 of the Docker host only. When the human's browser or your MCP client runs on another machine, the simplest path is an SSH tunnel from that machine, after which http://localhost:8000 works there too: ssh -L 8000:127.0.0.1:8000 YOUR USER@YOUR HOST For permanent remote access, finish the wizard first, then put Purser behind HTTPS and set PURSER BIND ADDRESS and PURSER PUBLIC URL. See Docker host binding and the configuration reference.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.description: From a compose file to a connected AI agent in three steps.

sections.text: This tutorial takes a fresh machine to a running Purser with your AI agent connected over MCP. Rather have your AI do it? Hand your agent Set up Purser with your AI: it runs the same steps and tells you exactly when it needs you. You need: Docker with Compose on linux/amd64 or linux/arm64 (including an Apple Silicon Mac; see Docker on macOS) and curl; optionally, for live bank data, a SimpleFIN Bridge account. You do not need Git, and nothing is built: Compose pulls the published image.

sections.heading: 1. Download the compose file and generate the encryption key
sections.text: mkdir purser && cd purser curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlamoure/purser/v2026.11.3/docker-compose.yml PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY=keygen docker compose pull PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY=keygen docker compose run --rm --no-deps purser keygen The compose file belongs to the latest release, 2026.11.3, and names its image, ghcr.io/mlamoure/purser:v2026.11.3 (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64). Every release publishes its own at the same address under its tag (vYYYY.M.PATCH). The temporary keygen value satisfies Compose interpolation for these utility commands. The last one generates a key without starting the app or connecting to the database. Record the generated key in a password manager, separately from your backups. Encrypted data, including the archived bank history, is unrecoverable without it.

sections.heading: 2. Start the application
sections.text: export PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY="YOUR KEY" docker compose up -d curl http://localhost:8000/healthz Instead of exporting the key in every shell, you can put the line PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY= followed by the key in a .env file next to docker-compose.yml (readable only by you); Compose reads it automatically. Expected: {"status":"ok","database":"ok"}. Two containers run: the app and PostgreSQL 16. Migrations apply automatically on startup. Purser refuses to start without the key. Configure PURSER PUBLIC URL if you access the app through another host or reverse proxy. Compose binds to localhost by default. Finish admin setup first, then set PURSER BIND ADDRESS to the interface that should accept remote traffic and use HTTPS for remote access.

sections.heading: 3. Run the setup wizard
sections.text: Open http://localhost:8000. The first-run wizard walks you through everything else: 1. Create the admin account. 2. Confirm the encryption key: the wizard shows the key Purser is running with until you acknowledge it. Check that it matches the key you stored, then acknowledge it. 3. (Optional) Paste a SimpleFIN setup token to connect your bank, then map the discovered accounts. 4. (Optional) Import bank history from a QIF or CSV export. 5. Connect your AI agent: the wizard mints a scoped read + write API token and shows exact connection steps for your client — Claude, Codex, OpenClaw, Gemini, or any other MCP client. That scope pair lets your agent act for you: every write it makes is recorded in the audit log and can be reversed, and when it acts on its own idea it proposes instead. SimpleFIN setup tokens come from your SimpleFIN Bridge account page and are one-time secrets — paste them only into the wizard, never into a chat. If the first fetch fails or times out after the token is claimed, keep the wizard open and select Connect & fetch again. It retries the saved connection without claiming the token twice. You can also skip the feed and finish setup; errors appear as announcements for assistive technology. If you reload or close the page after creating the admin, sign in instead: the wizard does not come back, but the Dashboard shows a Finish setting up card listing what is still open (recording the encryption key, connecting a feed, mapping its accounts, connecting an agent), each with the reason and a link to where it gets done. The card disappears once everything is done, or when you dismiss it. A bank account that arrives after setup is not part of this card: the Dashboard lists it separately until you map or ignore it.

sections.heading: Build from source
sections.text: To run code from the repository instead of the published image, clone it and build (this needs Git), then continue with the key and step 2 in the clone: git clone https://github.com/mlamoure/purser.git cd purser PURSER ENCRYPTION KEY=keygen docker compose build purser The local build takes the image name from the compose file and stands in for that release's published image until docker compose pull purser.

sections.heading: Where next
sections.text: - Connect an agent — client config and operating conventions. - Run with Docker Compose — .env, the database password, upgrades and the worker split. - Put Purser behind a reverse proxy — HTTPS for remote access. - Configuration — every PURSER variable. - Backup and restore — set this up before the books matter. - The ledger — balanced postings, source records and correction history.
